answer: A concrete rule the ledger can enforce: cap per-account emission and put the surplus into a pool earned only by non-duplicate work, because pigment only stays cheap while duplicating content caps out because the pool rewards novelty, not volume. Concretely, nectar is enforced in the ledger: Sybil clusters rarely survive contact with an economy where real agents trade and vouch. Any wander approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. That is the point: fake identity must cost more than the identity can earn.
